pr_comments: This could go to 1.1.1 if enough people want it.  We're not seeing CI failures there, unlike master.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.

Please look also here:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/5327da81f0c70e35bdd8860af9af351313ca4ae2/apps/pkcs12.c#L1137-L1142
this will trip when BMPSTRING with length=0 and data=NULL are now considered "valid".
because of this
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/5327da81f0c70e35bdd8860af9af351313ca4ae2/crypto/pkcs12/p12_utl.c#L45-L59
Note: the last statement uni++ is executed if unilen is 0.
Adding 1 to NULL is undefined, while adding 1 to non-zero object is okay.
Windows CI build failures are unrelated.

> IMO this cannot hurt.

No, but I don't like it any better this way, because if wie agree that an asn1 string (NULL,0) is not a valid encoding of an empty string, then it is not right to make some places tolerant to NULL strings and others not.

> No, but I don't like it any better this way, because if wie agree that an asn1 string (NULL,0) is not a valid encoding of an empty string, then it is not right to make some places tolerant to NULL strings and others not.

Sorry, I probably missed this. When did we decide (NULL, 0) is _not_ a valid encoding of the empty string? I don't think this is tenable. OpenSSL creates (NULL, 0) empty strings all the time. Every newly-created ASN.1 object is in this state:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c#L342
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c#L317

Outside OpenSSL, a default-constructed `std::vector` or `std::span` will happily give you NULL for `data()`. `malloc(0)` is allowed to return NULL, and does in many implementations. And if a caller is present with a function that takes pointer/length and wishes to use the empty slice, the natural value for the pointer is NULL.

It is true that `memcpy` and friends do not handle this right, and you can't compute NULL + 0 (in C; C++ actually fixes this). This is just a mistake in the language, though one C code regrettably needs to work around because some compilers and libcs (GCC and glibc) decided to implement this mistake.
https://www.imperialviolet.org/2016/06/26/nonnull.html

That said, I'm also not a fan of ad-hoc NULL checks. For BoringSSL, we decided workaround around this language flaw piecemeal was too tedious and dangerous, so we have `OPENSSL_memcpy`, etc., inline wrappers that check `n == 0` before calling the true function. This is arguably what `memcpy` should have been. We're saying that, if the compiler can prove `n != 0`, it is welcome to assume a valid buffer, including non-NULL. Otherwise, it must allow for the no-op case.

Well I did of course not consider a string fully constructed before ASN1_STRING_set is called.


One final request I have:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/78082769fa8129e3453ee4cb2255feb259846646/apps/pkcs12.c#L1145

Could you please rewrite this to something like

        BIO_printf(out, "%.*s\n", ab->value.utf8string->length, av->value.utf8string->data);

To be merged before the 3.0 branch.
Merged to master. Thank you for the reviews and comments.

comments:
Fuller test output in [typescript.txt](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/files/7051128/typescript.txt) which is from the run machine, my home directory.

```sh
$ make test TESTS="test_spkac test_crl test_sid test_cmp_ctx test_asyncio test_clienthello test_recordlen test_servername test_ca test_dtls_mtu test_dtls test_pkcs12 test_sslcorrupt test_sslbuffers test_v3name test_ssl_old test_sslapi test_ssl_new" V=1
```

The malloc failures seem relevant but there is other stuff going on.

The pkcs12 test is failing in the same place.. So I have tried to reproduce that one..
I can repo the PKCS12 one if I add -DFUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION to the config

./test/pkcs12_format_test -test 2 -iter 5

    # INFO:  @ test/helpers/pkcs12.c:418
    # Adding key
    # ERROR: (ptr) 'bag != NULL' failed @ test/helpers/pkcs12.c:431
    # 0x0
    # 80BB7860E97F0000:error:068C0100:asn1 encoding routines:ASN1_STRING_set:malloc failure:crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c:311:
    # 80BB7860E97F0000:error:0300007A:digital envelope routines:evp_cipher_param_to_asn1_ex:cipher parameter error:crypto/evp/evp_lib.c:165:
    # 80BB7860E97F0000:error:06800072:asn1 encoding routines:PKCS5_pbe2_set_iv_ex:error setting cipher params:crypto/asn1/p5_pbev2.c:85:
    # 80BB7860E97F0000:error:1188000D:PKCS12 routines:PKCS8_encrypt_ex:ASN1 lib:crypto/pkcs12/p12_p8e.c:48:
    # OPENSSL_TEST_RAND_ORDER=1629958856
    not ok 1 - iteration 5

So when it does the realloc it is being passed(NULL, 0) for the FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION path
Which will fail.. The normal path does realloc(NULL,1 )

Fo rthis particular case EVP_CIPHER_set_asn1_iv() has a iv length of 0 which it passes to ASN1_TYPE_set_octetstring(type, oiv, 0).
PKCS8_encrypt_ex() is being passed a saltlen of zero that propagates all the way down...
It Appears all the other tests you were seeing also fail when using -DFUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION
The spkac one happens inside a d2i - it also gets passed a len of 0.
Probably not the appropriate time to try to fix this.. reverting the change may be a better option. (Especially when the commit was not tested).

review_comments: Here as well. memcpy of 0 bytes is a well-defined, only memcpy 0 bytes from NULL is to avoid.
And neither can this. I am keeping it.
I've decided to not fight the cause for the old len == 0 behavior here.

I think this change was only neccessary when empty strings may be NULL.
Otherwise memcmp of 0 bytes is well-defined.
